minutes.headline: Commission ordered a West Street owner to undo drainage trenches and approved Hemlock Drive walls despite a grandfathering split.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a series of wetlands hearings: it approved a septic replacement, a retaining wall determination, a common driveway culvert crossing, and wall repairs at 72 Hemlock Drive after a debate over whether old wall remnants are grandfathered. It gave preliminary support to a conservation restriction for the 994 Northfield Road solar site and authorized paying for a 21E study from a trust fund. It ordered restoration of drainage trenches at 228 West Street and continued several hearings to January 15.

what_happened.line: The commission ordered the 228 West Street owner to restore drainage trenches to their original condition by spring, with notice to the agent first.
It approved a notice of intent for retaining walls at 72 Hemlock Drive, with the face of the wall staked and approved by the agent, after debate over grandfathering.
It approved the common driveway crossing at 41 and 47 Reservoir Road and the 69 Colburn Street septic replacement.
It approved the conservation restriction for the 994 Northfield Road solar site as drafted and backed sending it to the state.
Votes to pay for a 21E study from the land acquisition trust fund and to continue three hearings to January 15 were not audible in the minutes.

why_it_matters: The conservation restriction on the solar site and the choice to pay for the 21E study from the land acquisition trust fund, not the forestry account, bear on how town conservation money is used.
The Hemlock Drive and West Street decisions show how the commission treats old walls and altered drainage near wetlands, which affects what nearby property owners may build or must undo.
watch_next: Continued hearings for 54 Plantation Drive, the DPW culvert and the Nancy Bell retaining wall return on January 15.
A site inspection at 139 Northfield Road was planned for Saturday, January 11, and could slip to spring if snow covers the ground.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the general run of business: the same hearings, the January 15 continuations, the $100 fine, the $1,735 trust-fund transfer and the conservation restriction. They differ on several names and details, and our minutes leave many votes "not audible". The main thing to know is that the official minutes record a 4-2-1 split on the retaining wall vote and different dates for the 139 Northfield Road site inspection and the 228 West Street restoration, none of which our recording supports.
